public_rationale: Research shows that language-model-based robotic planning can improve with environmental feedback and additional planning components. That weighs against dismissing the approach outright. But selected successes do not establish dependable household operation, and remaining failures do not prove that limited world comprehension makes success impossible. The evidence does not settle the causal claim under the contextual reading of success.
limitations: The result depends on reading success as dependable household performance rather than any successful demonstration.
The cited studies do not directly measure the speaker's concept of world comprehension.
Later systems introduce components and capabilities that complicate comparisons with PaLM-SayCan.

our_interpretation: Read success in context as dependable, safe performance of varied household requests, rather than completion of a selected demonstration.
Read the claim as a causal objection: inadequate world understanding prevents dependable robot performance.
The speaker supplies neither a measurement of world comprehension nor a success threshold. Those omissions limit how strongly experiments can settle the claim.
Later research may inform the causal assessment, but success with a materially different architecture does not automatically refute a criticism of the 2022 approach.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled, representative evaluations establish that limited world understanding in the relevant language system prevents dependable household performance, after separating that limitation from perception, control, and hardware failures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Robots using the criticized kind of language system demonstrate sustained, independently verified, safe performance across varied household requests without overcoming the limitation alleged to prevent success.

evidence.explanation: The experiments show that language-model-based robotic planning can improve through environmental feedback. This challenges a blanket dismissal of the approach, but does not demonstrate dependable, safe household operation or isolate world comprehension as the decisive cause.

Later work reports improved household planning with additional memory and planning components, while substantial task failures remain. Its benchmark abstracts away physical control and uses a different system, so it cannot settle the claim about the criticized architecture.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative, repeated household evaluations with safety checks and controlled comparisons separating language understanding from perception, control, and added feedback, using explicit criteria for success and the system class being tested.
